svg.text: Everyday English - Idioms & slang
under the gun
MEANING
Under strong pressure, usually because a deadline is
close.
IN CONTEXT
We are under the gun to finish the proposal before the
client meeting.
USAGE NOTE
This is an informal American expression. It emphasizes
pressure, not literal danger. Under pressure is more
suitable for a formal report or a sensitive conversation.
Use under the gun to do something; avoid under a gun.
Be specific about the deadline so the listener
understands what help you need.
CONVERSATION
A: Can you review these slides today?
B: I can, but I am under the gun with another deadline.
A: Would tomorrow morning be more realistic?
B: Yes. Send them over and I will review them before
lunch.
YOUR TURN
Make this request considerate: We are under the gun,
so help us now. Model: We are under the gun to finish
by Friday. Would you have time to review one section
today?
